newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac gets red meat treat at farm show.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac gets red meat treat at farm show.

text.p: French butchers, eager to boost sluggish red meat sales after the mad cow crisis, presented President Jacques Chirac with a hefty T-bone steak on Sunday.
Chirac, who has stuck to his favourite tete de veau (calf's head stew) dish throughout the health scare that erupted last March, was making his annual trip to the opening of the Paris SIA farm show.
French butcher-apprentice Steve Prevost said he handed him a 1-5 kilo (three-pound) ready-to-cook T-bone steak from Chirac's central Limousin home region, where cattle feeds on grass.
French butchers, whose beef sales dipped by as much as 30 percent at the height of the mad cow crisis last year, said consumption has been making a modest comeback since December.
"Sales have been picking up since Christmas but are still below last year's levels," said Michel Colin, a teacher at the Paris and lle-de-France professional butcher school.
He said that the farm show, due to last until next Sunday, provided the meat industry with a good opportunity to reassure confused consumers that it was safe to eat red meat again.
"The fair allows us to show our know-how and efforts made to promote quality," Colin said.
France was the first nation to ban imports of British beef after Britain announced a possible link between Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) and the deadly human Creutzfeldt Jacob Disease (CJD).
Statistics from the national meat board OFIVAL show beef sales fell 10 percent in 1996 from 1995. Last month's sales were still lagging eight to 10 percent below their year-ago level.
Chirac, a former farm minister with a strong backing among rural voters, did not disappoint his fans, tasting regional foods, patting cows and kissing children in a two-and-a-half-hour marathon tour.
"He is a connoisseur," said Guy Chastenet, a breeder from Tulle, in the Correze region where Chirac grew up.
"We know him well. He is from Correze like us. When he discusses animals, he knows what he is talking about," he added.
